name: breakdown_rollup_region_and_country_subtotals
input:
SELECT region, country, SUM(fatalities) AS fatalities
FROM acled.global_events
WHERE week >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND week < DATE '2026-01-01'
  AND region IN ('Eastern Africa', 'Middle Africa')
GROUP BY ROLLUP (region, country)
ORDER BY region NULLS LAST, country NULLS LAST

additional_metadata.notes: Fatalities in 2025 for each Eastern and Middle African country, with a subtotal for each region and a grand total. GROUP BY ROLLUP adds rows a plain GROUP BY wouldn't: one per region with country NULL (its subtotal), and one with both NULL (the grand total). NULLS LAST puts each region's subtotal after its countries and the grand total last. 31 rows: 28 countries, 2 subtotals, 1 total. A breakdown must explain the extra rows and what the NULLs mean; country is never NULL in the data, so a NULL always marks a total.

name: breakdown_chained_ctes_with_ranking
input:
WITH weekly AS (
  SELECT country, week, SUM(fatalities) AS fatalities
  FROM acled.global_events
  WHERE event_type = 'Battles'
  GROUP BY country, week
),
yearly AS (
  SELECT country, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM week) AS year,
    SUM(fatalities) AS fatalities, MAX(fatalities) AS worst_week
  FROM weekly
  GROUP BY country, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM week)
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT country, year, fatalities, worst_week,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY fatalities DESC) AS rank_in_year
  FROM yearly
)
SELECT country, year, fatalities, worst_week, rank_in_year
FROM ranked
WHERE rank_in_year <= 5
ORDER BY year, rank_in_year

additional_metadata.notes: Three chained CTEs then a filter on the ranking: sections in order, each described correctly.

name: breakdown_new_high_weeks_share_of_region
input:
WITH weekly AS (
  SELECT country, week, SUM(events) AS events
  FROM acled.global_events
  WHERE event_type = 'Explosions/Remote violence'
    AND week >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND week < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY country, week
),
flagged AS (
  SELECT country, week, events,
    MAX(events) OVER (
      PARTITION BY country ORDER BY week
      ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
    ) AS prior_max
  FROM weekly
)
SELECT c.region,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.country) AS countries,
  COUNT(f.week) AS new_high_weeks,
  COUNT(DISTINCT f.country) * 100 / COUNT(DISTINCT c.country) AS pct_countries_with_new_high
FROM acled.countries c
LEFT JOIN flagged f
  ON f.country = c.country
 AND f.events > f.prior_max
GROUP BY c.region
ORDER BY pct_countries_with_new_high DESC, c.region NULLS LAST

additional_metadata.notes: For each region: how many countries it has, how many weeks of 2025 a country set a new high for explosion/remote violence events, and the percentage of its countries that set at least one. weekly totals each country's explosion events per week of 2025, with a row only for weeks that had some. In flagged the window ends one row before the current one, so prior_max is the most of any earlier such week; the ON clause keeps a week only if it beat that strictly, so a country's first week (prior_max NULL) never counts and equalling the high doesn't either: Guatemala's four weeks of 1 event and Syria's second week of 128 after 128 are no new highs. 110 new-high weeks in 51 countries; counting first weeks gives 199 in all 89 countries with explosions, and >= gives 249. The LEFT JOIN with that test in ON keeps every country (251), so COUNT(DISTINCT c.country) is all of a region's countries and COUNT(f.week) is 0 for one without a new high (COUNT(*) would count 1): the percentage is of all countries, not of those with explosions (Middle East 9 of 15 is 60, not 9 of 11). Integer division rounds the percentage down: Northern Africa's 4 of 6 is 66, not 67. Countries with no region form a group of their own (7 countries, 0), sorted last among the 0s. 19 rows.

name: breakdown_case_buckets_with_subquery
input:
SELECT country, fatalities,
  CASE
    WHEN fatalities >= 1000 THEN 'High'
    WHEN fatalities >= 100 THEN 'Medium'
    ELSE 'Low'
  END AS fatality_level
FROM acled.reported_fatalities
WHERE year = 2024
  AND country IN (SELECT country FROM acled.countries WHERE region = 'Western Africa')
ORDER BY fatalities DESC

additional_metadata.notes: Explains the three categories and the Western Africa filter.

name: breakdown_spike_weeks_window_before_current
input:
WITH weekly AS (
  SELECT country, week, SUM(events) AS events
  FROM acled.global_events
  WHERE region = 'Middle East'
    AND week >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  GROUP BY country, week
),
with_prior AS (
  SELECT country, week, events,
    AVG(events) OVER (
      PARTITION BY country ORDER BY week
      ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
    ) AS prior_avg
  FROM weekly
)
SELECT country, week, events, ROUND(prior_avg, 1) AS prior_avg
FROM with_prior
WHERE events > 2 * prior_avg
ORDER BY country, week

additional_metadata.notes: Weeks in which a Middle East country had more than twice the average of its previous three weeks of events, since 2025. The window ends one row before the current one, so a week is compared with the weeks before it; a country's first week has no average, so it never counts; and the three rows are the previous weeks with events, not necessarily the previous three calendar weeks. 61 rows.

name: breakdown_union_and_correlated_having
input:
SELECT c.region, COUNT(*) AS busy_countries
FROM (
  SELECT country FROM acled.demonstration_events_country
  WHERE year = 2024 AND events > 500
  UNION
  SELECT country FROM acled.political_violence_year
  WHERE year = 2024 AND events > 500
) busy
JOIN acled.countries c ON c.country = busy.country
GROUP BY c.region
HAVING COUNT(*) > (
  SELECT COUNT(*) / 4.0
  FROM acled.countries c2
  WHERE c2.region = c.region
)
ORDER BY busy_countries DESC

additional_metadata.notes: Regions where more than a quarter of the countries were 'busy' in 2024: over 500 demonstration events or over 500 political violence events. UNION, not UNION ALL, so a country busy in both counts once (66 countries, not 80 rows). The HAVING subquery is correlated: it counts the countries of each region in turn, so the threshold differs by region. 8 regions.

name: breakdown_lateral_top3_weeks_per_country
input:
SELECT c.country, t.week, t.fatalities
FROM acled.countries c
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT g.week, SUM(g.fatalities) AS fatalities
  FROM acled.global_events g
  WHERE g.country = c.country
    AND g.week >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  GROUP BY g.week
  ORDER BY fatalities DESC
  LIMIT 3
) t
WHERE c.region = 'Eastern Africa'
ORDER BY c.country, t.fatalities DESC

additional_metadata.notes: Each Eastern African country's three deadliest weeks since the start of 2025. The LATERAL subquery runs once per country; CROSS JOIN LATERAL would drop a country with no events since 2025 (none in Eastern Africa today); ties at the third week are broken arbitrarily. 57 rows.

name: breakdown_filter_share_with_nullif
input:
WITH totals AS (
  SELECT country,
    SUM(fatalities) AS fatalities,
    COALESCE(SUM(fatalities) FILTER (WHERE event_type = 'Violence against civilians'), 0) AS civilian_fatalities
  FROM acled.global_events
  WHERE country IN ('Sudan', 'Myanmar', 'Mexico', 'Nigeria', 'Ukraine', 'Haiti')
    AND week >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND week < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY country
)
SELECT country, fatalities, civilian_fatalities,
  ROUND(100.0 * civilian_fatalities / NULLIF(fatalities, 0), 1) AS civilian_share
FROM totals
ORDER BY civilian_share DESC NULLS LAST

additional_metadata.notes: Six countries' 2025 fatalities, those from violence against civilians, and that share as a percentage. FILTER sums only the violence-against-civilians rows while fatalities still counts every event type, so it is a share of all deaths (a WHERE on the event type would make both columns the same: Ukraine's 78,121 would become 86). COALESCE makes a country with no such rows 0 rather than NULL; NULLIF stops a division by zero, leaving the share NULL for a country with no fatalities, and NULLS LAST sorts those last. Neither guard fires today: all six have fatalities. 6 rows, from Mexico (80.4%) to Ukraine (0.1%).

name: breakdown_not_in_with_null_in_the_list
input:
SELECT DISTINCT region
FROM acled.countries
WHERE region NOT IN (
  SELECT c.region
  FROM acled.countries c
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM acled.reported_fatalities r
    WHERE r.country = c.country AND r.year = 2024
  )
)
ORDER BY region

additional_metadata.notes: Meant as the regions in which every country has a 2024 reported-fatalities record: the subquery lists the regions of countries with no 2024 record, and NOT IN keeps the other regions. But it returns no rows: 7 of the 33 countries with no 2024 record have no region, so the list contains NULL, and NOT IN against a list containing NULL is never true. Written with NOT EXISTS, or with region IS NOT NULL in the subquery, it returns 9 regions. A breakdown that says it finds the regions where every country has a record, without the NULL problem, describes a result the query never gives.

name: breakdown_join_actors_sanctions
input:
WITH sides AS (
  SELECT side_a AS side FROM ucdp.ucdp_ged WHERE country_id = 626 AND year = 2024
  UNION
  SELECT side_b FROM ucdp.ucdp_ged WHERE country_id = 626 AND year = 2024
)
SELECT s.side, m.side IS NOT NULL AS on_sanctions_list
FROM sides s
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT s2.side
  FROM sides s2
  JOIN opensanctions_public.os_targets t ON lower(t.name) = lower(s2.side)
) m ON m.side = s.side
ORDER BY s.side

additional_metadata.notes: Every actor (side_a or side_b) in South Sudan's 2024 UCDP events, and whether a sanctioned target has exactly the same name, ignoring case. The CTE lists the actors once each (UNION removes duplicates). The subquery joins them to os_targets on lower(name) = lower(side), and DISTINCT keeps each matched actor once however many targets share its name. The LEFT JOIN keeps actors with no match, and m.side IS NOT NULL turns that into true or false. 19 rows, all false today: the sanctions list names these parties differently. A breakdown must say the match is on the exact name (case aside), not a similar one, and why actors with no match still appear. Plain PostgreSQL: an earlier version used pg_trgm's % and similarity(), which a plain PostgreSQL database doesn't have.
